background: Former Duke point guard and Missouri head coach (1999-2006) who rebuilt his career through the D-League (Austin Toros) and assistant stops with the 76ers, Lakers, CSKA Moscow and Hawks before an eight-season run as Utah Jazz head coach (2014-15 to 2021-22, 372-264, six straight playoff trips, two Coach of the Year runner-up finishes but never past the second round). Resigned from Utah in June 2022, then was hired by Atlanta in February 2023 on a five-year deal. In Atlanta he inherited a Trae Young-centric roster, remade it into a fast-paced, ball-movement team (league-leading, franchise-record 30.1 assists per game in 2025-26), won the 2025-26 Southeast Division at 46-36 and received a second multi-year extension in June 2026 after a first-round loss to the eventual champion Knicks. Career regular-season record roughly 504-399 entering 2026-27, fifth-most wins among active coaches.

prior_head_coaching.notes: Six consecutive playoff appearances (2017-2022), 0 conference finals; drop-coverage defense built around Rudy Gobert and a top-3 three-point-volume offense (2020-21 Jazz 52-20, No. 1 seed in West). COY runner-up 2017-18 and 2020-21. Resigned June 2022.
Elite Eight in 2002; resigned in 2006 amid NCAA investigation.

evidence: Traditionally favored a nine-man rotation in Utah (Salt City Hoops, 2020).

In Atlanta 2025-26 he talked up the roster's versatility and 'endless lineup options' but still left breakout players (Krejci, Gueye) out of the rotation to start the year (Soaring Down South, 2025-26).
Trae Young and Jalen Johnson both averaged roughly 36 mpg when healthy in 2023-24 and 2024-25 (background knowledge; not re-verified via search).
In Utah, Mitchell and Gobert routinely played 33-34 mpg with heavy playoff loads.
Snyder's own stated philosophy: 'Any time you start changing things too much, it doesn't give a certain group of guys the opportunity to find a rhythm together' (Utah, 2020).
But Atlanta beat coverage in 2025-26 called his back-end rotation decisions 'baffling' and said he had 'lost the knack for building a rotation'.
Started No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher all of 2024-25 and leaned on 22-year-olds Daniels and Johnson as co-stars (background knowledge).
Yet young breakout players Vit Krejci and Mouhamed Gueye began 2025-26 outside the rotation, and in Utah he was slow to trust young reserves (Exum, Tucker) over veterans.

Rarely sits healthy stars; the one documented 2024-25 case of holding starters out late (vs Charlotte) was framed around injuries and short bodies: 'guys were chipped maybe ten minutes off what they regularly play'.
Trae Young played 70+ games in each full healthy season under Snyder (background knowledge).

Uses matchup-based closers (Daniels for defense, Kennard for spacing), which drew criticism when Kennard stayed on late vs Brooklyn in 2024-25 and when Trae Young sat during a decisive stretch vs Chicago (Dec 2025).
Trae-less closing units with Johnson/Daniels/Alexander-Walker were used during Young's 2025-26 absence.
Hawks played at the league's third-fastest pace (103.4) in 2024-25 (VSiN preview, 2025).
2025 training camp was centered on 'capitalizing on transition opportunities'; AJC: 'Hawks focus on ball movement to play at a faster pace' (2024-25).
Utah teams under Snyder were top-3 in 3PA (No. 1 in 2020-21), but his first Hawks teams attempted only 30.5 3PA/g (28th, 2022-23) and 'instead the offense pushed inward toward the rim' in 2024-25.
2025-26 roster (Porzingis, Kennard, Alexander-Walker) was built to raise volume; previews projected 'more threes, more pace'.
2025-26 Hawks averaged a franchise-record, league-leading 30.1 assists per game (NBA.com, June 2026).
Snyder deliberately moved away from a Trae Young-centric offense, using Young as a decoy and running actions through Jalen Johnson (2024-25).
Top-3 pace in 2024-25 driven by Daniels' steals and Johnson grab-and-go; camp emphasis on transition in Sept 2025.
Snyder's Utah teams were slower and half-court oriented, so the transition emphasis is roster-driven rather than dogmatic.
Utah under Snyder consistently ranked near the bottom in offensive rebound rate, prioritizing transition defense (background knowledge, not re-verified).
Atlanta has had crashers in Capela/Okongwu but no reporting found on an explicit crash-the-glass emphasis.
Boston Globe (April 2023): 'Hawks are built inside out'; 2024-25 offense 'pushed inward toward the rim' with high rim frequency rather than post-ups.
Porzingis added some post/high-post play in 2025-26 but the system is drive-and-kick, not post-centric.
Widely described as an 'innovative' X-and-O coach whose actions make the offense 'harder to predict' (CelticsBlog, 2023 playoff preview).
Long-standing league reputation from Utah as one of the best set-play designers; Spurs reportedly viewed him as a preferred Popovich successor.
Hawks 2024-25 led the league in steals/deflections behind Dyson Daniels; scheme described as drop bigs 'supported by aggressive perimeter defense' (2025).
Snyder's Utah defenses were conservative Gobert-drop units that forced few turnovers, so his aggressiveness is personnel-dependent.
Hawks were second-to-last in opponent 3P% two straight seasons (2023-24, 2024-25) and early in 2025-26 gave up the most 3PA per game before tightening (SI, 2025-26).
Utah's deep-drop scheme famously conceded above-the-break threes to protect the rim; 2025 preview: Porzingis lets him 'make drop work in doses'.
Salt Lake Tribune (2018): Snyder 'turned a foul-happy Jazz team into one that fouls smartly, not frequently'.
Hawks have been roughly middle-of-pack in opponent free-throw rate under Snyder (background knowledge; foul trouble vs OKC in 2025-26 noted).
No reporting surfaced on regular zone usage; Hawks have mixed in occasional zone possessions but Snyder is a man-to-man drop/switch coach by reputation (inferred).
'We changed our pick-and-roll coverage, that's what happened' - Snyder after adjusting on Tyrese Maxey with Daniels guarding up (2025-26).
Previews noted he 'won't live in drop every night' and uses pre-switching and help concepts to shield Trae Young in PnR.
Let Dejounte Murray play through for a game-winning buzzer-beater rather than stopping play (Jan 2024); Snyder called the no-timeout choice 'always a debate'.
Criticized for not reinserting Trae Young after a Chicago timeout with a 6-point lead and 5:44 left (Dec 2025), suggesting he manages stoppages passively rather than reactively.
No direct evidence found on fouling-up-three tendencies; estimate at league average.
Typically closes with his starters plus one matchup piece (Daniels/Kennard); no evidence of unusually deep clutch rotations (inferred).
No published data on Snyder's challenge frequency or success rate was found; estimate league average.
Analytics-forward program in Utah routinely hunted end-of-quarter 2-for-1s (background impression, unverified).
Tends toward process-driven, measured choices (e.g., letting Murray play through without a timeout); no documented pattern of going-for-the-win gambles.
Respected tactician but with a history of late-game second-guessing: Trae-on-bench vs Bulls (Dec 2025), Kennard left in vs Nets (2024-25), Utah's 2021 collapse vs the Clippers.
AJC after 2026 playoffs: Knicks 'made adjustments in a way the Hawks couldn't match'.
In-game: changed PnR coverage mid-game vs Philadelphia (2025-26) and pivoted the whole offense away from Trae-centrism.

In-series: lost to the Knicks after Game 4 when, by his own words, 'it wasn't a game of adjustments as much as it was the team that got after it'; AJC said the Knicks adjusted in ways Atlanta could not match; Jazz-era series losses carried similar criticism.
Oversaw Donovan Mitchell and Rudy Gobert's rise in Utah; in Atlanta, Jalen Johnson's leap and Dyson Daniels' 2024-25 Most Improved Player / DPOY runner-up season.
AJC (April 2026): Snyder 'deserves heaps of credit for the Hawks turnaround'.
Utah under Snyder was a model 'threes and layups' analytics offense (No. 1 in 3PA in 2020-21); Atlanta's shift to rim pressure plus league-leading assists reflects shot-quality emphasis.
Hawks ran the third-fastest pace and a modern Trae-decoy system; Snyder publicly frames problems in process terms (turnovers, shot quality).
504 career wins (5th among active coaches), two COY runner-up finishes, reportedly San Antonio's preferred Popovich successor; second Hawks extension in June 2026.
Counter-narrative: never past the second round in 12 seasons and was described as 'on thin ice' entering 2025-26 before the 20-6 finish.

key_criticisms: Never advanced past the second round in 12 seasons as an NBA head coach; 2026 first-round loss to the Knicks framed as being out-adjusted and out-worked.
Back-end rotation choices in Atlanta called 'baffling' by beat coverage (Krejci/Gueye initially out of the rotation; questionable late-game personnel vs Bulls and Nets).
Three-point defense has been a chronic weakness: second-to-last in opponent 3P% in both 2023-24 and 2024-25.
Turnover-prone, high-pace offense that Snyder himself said 'puts us in a tough position' (2025-26).
key_strengths: Elite half-court set and ATO designer with a reputation as one of the league's most innovative X-and-O coaches.
Transformed Atlanta from a heliocentric Trae Young offense into the league's leading ball-movement team (30.1 apg in 2025-26) while keeping a top-3 pace.
Player development track record: Mitchell, Gobert, Jalen Johnson, Dyson Daniels (2025 MIP), Risacher.
Strong defensive pedigree from Utah (fouls 'smartly, not frequently'; drop-coverage mastery) that he has begun to port to Atlanta with Porzingis.
research_notes: Records: 2025-26 (46-36, lost R1 2-4 to NYK) and 2024-25 (40-42, play-in exit) confirmed by multiple sources; 2023-24 confirmed as 36-46 (not 36-44). Two career-win totals appear in June 2026 coverage (500-396 vs 504); 504 is consistent with the season-by-season sums. Precise 2025-26 pace, 3PA-rate and offensive-rebound rankings were not retrievable (stats sites blocked); 3PA volume for 2025-26 is uncertain.
